title: A finitely generated counterexample to the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture
main_claim: Let G be the Bestvina–Brady height kernel of the RAAG on a flag triangulation L of the acyclic presentation complex <x,y | x^2=y^5, x^2=(xy^{-1})^3>, whose fundamental group is the binary icosahedral group. Then G is finitely generated and residually finite, with cd G = 2 and gd G = 3, which would disprove the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture. Proof outline: (i) Presentation comparison theorem: suppose Γ is residually finite with a 2-dim K(Γ,1), and the boundary chains of a finite word list D form a free basis of the cycle module. Then any SU(2) edge labelling that is close enough to 1 and flat on D has trivial holonomy. (ii) Transport: pulling back a nontrivial representation π1(L)→SU(2) along slowly varying direction maps X^(1)→L gives labels that are uniformly small, flat on every triangle, and have nontrivial holonomy.
coverage:
Read all sections in full (introduction, degree, presentation, geometry, transport, conclusion). Checked by hand:
- Seed SU(2) representation: x^2 = y^5 = -1, and Re(xy^{-1}) = 1/2, so (xy^{-1})^3 = -1.
- Seed exponent matrix has determinant 1.
- Standard BB parts: cube complex, ascending/descending links, Mayer–Vietoris acyclicity of the level set, free action with finitely many orbits, cd = 2 via a Z^2 subgroup.
- Trace normal form and the direction-map Lipschitz bound 2/(n+1); edge images have diameter ≤ 4/N and triangle images ≤ 8/N.
- Exact subdivision along the commuting-power paths, closure of the concatenated loop, and the telescoping holonomy D(ξ)^{-1}α(γ)D(ξ).
- Shear algebra: PQP = [[0, A^{-1}], [-A, 0]], D0·PQP = [[0, 1], [-A, 0]], and the ordinary projection diag(1, -A) is an isomorphism.
- Exact-counts injectivity argument, and the quadratic estimate constants (conjugation-removal cost, interchange cost 2h^2, the T_0 bound).
- Threshold exclusion of h = δ.
- Localized degree lemma: the C_p fixed set is J^m; no mixed derivative blocks; the normal block is complex linear and so has positive real determinant; free orbits contribute multiples of p. Sanity checks: O = H^m gives det B, and the orbit of a non-central torus root gives b = 2.
- Degree continuation with moving open sets, and the finite-quotient copying via injectivity on P.
- Compactness of the arbitrary product and the final quadratic squeeze h ≤ C(δ+η)h.
No numerical computation beyond the seed check was needed. No step was found to fail. Confidence is moderate because the claim is extraordinary; the most delicate novel parts (Lemma 2.1 and Lemma 3.5 / Theorem 3.1) deserve an expert's second look.
